batch.short: One cycle of the control clock (dspClk). Every time in the controller is a whole number of batches. On the x6y3 build one batch is 2 ns and carries 16 DAC samples.

core.short: A small RISC-V processor (RV32I) that runs the firmware for a group of channels. It never plays samples itself; it writes registers that schedule them.

channel.short: The hardware next to a converter that holds a pulse table and timed queues and turns scheduled entries into samples. Kinds: pulse (DAC), demod (ADC) and dio (digital lines).

posted write.short: A store that the core sends and forgets: it travels over the link to a channel register without waiting for an answer.

pulse table.short: A channel's list of pulse entries, each with amplitude, phase, envelope address and duration. Firing writes an entry's index.

fire.short: Writing an entry index to a channel's fire register. The entry is queued to start at the channel's start time.

lead.short: How far ahead of its start time the firmware issues a write: 96 batches in RISC-Q's software. It covers the link, the queues and the slowest parameter path.

timed queue.short: A queue that releases each parameter at its start time minus that parameter's own pipeline latency, so all parameters of a pulse land on the same batch.

link.short: The pipelined path that carries posted writes from a core to its channels, and reports back. Its depth is counted in register stages.

hub.short: The board hub: shared bits (groups), counted barriers and mailboxes between cores. It passes one message per batch for the whole board.

barrier.short: A meeting point for cores. Each arrives and waits; the last arrival releases all of them with one common time.

sink.short: A core-local register that receives reports from a channel: a readout result, or a queue of input-line events.

DAC.short: Digital-to-analog converter: turns samples into a voltage on a wire.

ADC.short: Analog-to-digital converter: samples a returning signal, for example a readout tone.

NCO.short: Numerically controlled oscillator: a phase accumulator that generates a carrier frequency in digital logic.

carrier.short: The sinusoid a pulse is modulated onto. Its frequency is a 16-bit code in a channel register.

envelope.short: The shape of a pulse's amplitude over time, read from envelope memory.

demodulation.short: Multiplying a returning signal by a reference tone and integrating it over a window, to get one complex number per measurement.

readout.short: Measuring a qubit: a tone on its resonator, a demodulation window on the ADC, and a threshold that gives one bit.

feed-forward.short: Choosing a later operation from a measured bit during the same run.

virtual Z.short: A Z rotation done by shifting the phase of later pulses instead of playing a pulse.

transmon.short: A superconducting qubit made from a Josephson junction shunted by a capacitor, driven by microwave pulses of tens of nanoseconds.

QCCD.short: Quantum charge-coupled device: a trapped-ion architecture in which ions are moved between zones of a segmented trap.

shuttle.short: Moving an ion from one trap site to another by changing electrode voltages.

AOD.short: Acousto-optic deflector: a crystal in which an RF tone deflects a laser beam. The tone's frequency sets the beam's position.

tweezer.short: A tightly focused laser beam that holds one neutral atom.

Rydberg.short: A highly excited atomic state whose strong interaction gives neutral atoms their two-qubit gate.

Mølmer–Sørensen.short: The standard two-qubit gate on trapped ions, driven through the ions' shared motion.

syndrome.short: The measured parities of an error-correcting code. They reveal errors without revealing the encoded state.

decoder.short: The classical algorithm that turns syndromes into a correction.

union-find.short: A fast decoder that grows clusters around syndrome defects and merges them until each holds an even number.

Pauli frame.short: A classical record of Pauli corrections that are tracked in software instead of being applied as pulses.

system call.short: A service of the fault-tolerant operating system, such as decode_syndrome or route, with one latency and one capacity.

trace.short: The list of frames the Lean model emits as it executes: one frame per event, with an ID, a part, its causes and its state.

frame.short: One event of the trace: an instruction, a register write, a pulse window, a hub message or a signal reaching a qubit.

causal chain.short: The frames that led to a frame, following each frame's parents back to the firmware instruction that started it.

hardware instruction.short: One timed physical operation of a platform: a pulse, an ion shuttle, an AOD move, a measurement.

firmware.short: The RV32I machine code each control core runs.

Lean.short: A programming language and proof assistant. The controller model is written in Lean, so it runs and its properties can be proved.

preroll.short: Extra batches by which a segment starts later, so that the widest burst of simultaneous writes can still be issued on time.

put window.short: Core addresses from 0x10000 upward. A store there becomes a posted write to node n at 0x10000 + n·0x10000: nodes 0–15 are the core's channels, 16–19 hub groups, 20–35 barriers, 36 and up mailboxes.

dspClk.short: The converter-side clock of a RISC-Q build. One cycle is one batch: 500 MHz on the x6y3 build.

start time.short: The channel register (+0x4100) holding the batch at which the next fired entry starts. A fire advances it by the entry's duration.

arbiter.short: The round-robin stage of the board hub. It passes one message per batch for the whole board, from a queue of eight per core.

link depth.short: The number of register stages of the posted link. A write reaches its channel 1 + link depth batches after the store.

host window.short: Write-only core addresses from 0x40000000 through which firmware reports results to the host computer.

mailbox.short: One of two core-local registers (0x4340, 0x4360) that receive a word sent through the hub to that core alone. A load stalls until a word arrives.

effect frame.short: The trace frame in which a converter's output reaches an apparatus part, with its arrival time after the wire delay.

decoding graph.short: A graph with one node per check per round and one edge per possible error. A decoder groups the defects on it.

defect.short: A node of the decoding graph whose check changed value: the input a decoder starts from.

reaction time.short: The time from a measurement to the moment an operation that depends on its decoded result can start.

segment.short: A stretch of a compiled program that all active cores start together after a barrier, with one shared time base.

hyperfine qubit.short: A qubit stored in two hyperfine levels of an atom's or ion's electronic ground state, which makes it very insensitive to noise.

dispersive readout.short: Measuring a transmon through a coupled resonator whose frequency shifts with the qubit state, so a probe tone returns with a state-dependent amplitude and phase.

DRAG.short: A pulse-shaping correction that adds a derivative component on the quadrature channel, so a short pulse does not excite the second excited level.

RFSoC.short: A chip that combines fast DACs and ADCs, FPGA logic and ARM processors. RISC-Q targets AMD's ZCU216 board.

Nyquist frequency.short: Half the sample rate: the highest frequency a converter represents without an image.

surface code.short: An error-correcting code with one logical qubit in a d × d patch of qubits and d² − 1 checks between neighbours.

MWPM.short: Minimum-weight perfect matching: a decoder that pairs detection events so that the total weight of the connecting paths is minimal.

SLM.short: Spatial light modulator: shapes one laser beam into a fixed pattern of tweezers.

White Rabbit.short: CERN's Ethernet-based protocol for sub-nanosecond time distribution between boards. RISC-Q has a node for it; this model does not.
